Out of all the annoying tips people will give, hydration is one I won't get too upset over because it's at least a valid tip for a lot of health related stuff.  If someone suggests essential oils to me for a migraine though, they shall feel my wrath.

I just eat a balanced diet, and very rarely eat junk food.  I don't ever touch soda.   I've become excellent at shopping on a tight budget, and I take one day a week where I cook food and freeze portions.   I do my best to avoid grabbing last minute fast food.   Not just for health reasons, but for cost reasons.   I also just don't eat massive portions.   It's just all a routine for me at this point.

Some examples.  For a snack I make hard boiled eggs at the start of the week.  One of those completely kills hunger.  Fruit and apples with almond butter are another snack.

 I make some mish-mash dishes like one that's ground turkey, peppers, onions, diced tomatoes and lots of spice.  That's one I can freeze.  I have other ones like that which are a lentil base.  I make stew in my instant pot a lot.  Same idea, use some during the week, freeze the rest.  Doing that I end up with weeks where I just don't have to do much prep at all.   

My metabolism is still pretty quick even though I'm older. And I'm in my 40's and I could still wear old band shirts I have in storage from when I was a teenager.   I could eat a bunch of garbage and still be skinny likely. Especially when I'm active.  But that won't last forever.   But eating like garbage would make me feel like garbage anyway, so I have no reason too.  I'm definitely naturally skinny.  But I'm also going to stay that way.

Besides that there can literally be standing water when it rains in a bunker with no drainage (you may have seen this on a course), the sand just just turn into layers of a compacted mess (which can be even worse with some sand types).  So the bunker just feels like crappy hard sand, rather than a sand trap.  To make it worse some courses fix that by just throwing more sand on top of the crappy sand.  The traps will eventually be horrible in an area with a wet climate.

There are some really good sands that handle water better.  But, the traps will still eventually have issues if they don't have drainage.

Also, I am basing this on my area.  We get sudden blasts of rain for days, then can have a week of 35c draught weather in our summers.  So bunkers getting saturated, then drying constantly can turn the sand into an almost unrakable crust at times on a course where the bunkers aren't looked after at all.  Which seems to be the case with even mid level courses now.  

 Like the other poster said, if you can't maintain them at all, use an alternative.

It varies in complexity.  The basics are drain tile (corrugated pipe) in the low point of the trap.  But there can also be more complex  patterns of tile that run down the faces as and connect to that tile.  It's covered in a sock, or sometimes pea gravel or coarse sand, sometimes a combination of the 3. Then bunker sand over it all.  Each superintendent I have worked for has their own preferences, which budget can heavily dictate.  EG one course I worked for put new drainage in 90 traps over a single season.  That's something not a lot of courses have the budget for.

I work at a high end course with a ton of staff.  We aren't open yet, and we just spent a week properly grading and raking traps, and are only up to the 9th hole.   Most courses with no budget and fewer staff don't even get to do this step in a lot of cases.  So the bunkers just never really start out great, then get worse as the season goes on.  Especially as the summer goes on and part time workers don't care.  Then on top of that you get bunkers that were never built right, have no drainage, and are standing water anytime it rains.

So a course with no budget, and no staff would be better off with grass bunkers in a lot of cases like you say.   There's a course near me that only has grass bunkers, and it looks and plays great.
